mainTopic: The rules of כלל and פרט (and מיעט וריבה) applied to חיה and to a נזיר, and רבי יוחנן's rule that היתר combines with איסור only for a נזיר
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבא's statement that a חיה is included in the category of בהמה. רב יהודה מדיסקרתא challenges him. The פסוק names only cattle and sheep, so by the rules of פרט and כלל only things like those examples are included. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about spending מעשר שני money as the source for the rule that we include only things similar to the detail. It then asks why a כלל ופרט וכלל needs its last כלל, and why a פרט וכלל ופרט needs its last פרט, and answers both. Next it explains how these two methods differ: one needs similarity in only one way, the other in two ways. It also compares פרט וכלל with מיעט וריבה, using the leaves and tendrils of the vine forbidden to a נזיר. Finally, רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן: in all Torah prohibitions, permitted food does not combine with forbidden food toward the minimum amount, except for a נזיר, learned from the word ״משרת״.

steps.title: A wild animal is included in the category of animal
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of רבא's statement: חיה falls under the general category of בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wild animal is included in the category of 'animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last words of רבא's statement. He says the word בהמה also covers a חיה (a wild, undomesticated animal).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is reading the general category broadly. On his reading, a פסוק that speaks about animals would include wild animals too, not only farm animals. This broad reading is what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild, undomesticated animal (like a deer)
An animal; usually a domesticated farm animal
Included in, part of the category of

phrases.english: A wild animal is included in the category of animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חיה is included within the category of בהמה.

steps.title: The listed examples are cattle and sheep, so only similar things are included
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא challenges רבא. The פסוק says בקר וצאן, and by the rule of פרט וכלל (detail, generalization, detail) we only include things like the details, and a חיה is not like them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is a wild animal really included in 'animal'? But it is written 'cattle and sheep.' That makes a detail and a generalization, and you may only include things similar to the detail!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מדיסקרתא pushes back on רבא. The פסוק names only cattle and sheep, so how can you stretch it to include wild animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack uses the rule of interpreting generalizations and details. When a פסוק gives a general phrase together with specific examples, we include only things that resemble the examples. Cattle and sheep are farm animals, so a חיה would be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (starts a reply or challenge)
But it is written! (brings a פסוק as a challenge)
A detail; a specific item named in the פסוק
A generalization; a broad, general phrase
Similar to the detail

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge says a חיה is never a בהמה in any context. It only says that in this particular פסוק the named examples limit what is included.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה מדיסקרתא speaking to רבא.

phrases.english: A wild animal is included in animal?
But it is written 'cattle and sheep,'
and so it is a detail and a generalization,
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק is built detail, generalization, detail, so the named examples limit what it covers.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט!
phrases.english: and you may only include things similar to the detail!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חַיָּה בִּכְלַל בְּהֵמָה? הָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבא's claim from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that חיה is included in בהמה in this פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's examples (cattle, sheep) are farm animals. Because the פסוק is built as פרט וכלל (detail, generalization, detail), only items similar to the examples are included, so a wild animal is left out.

steps.title: Where do we learn that only similar things are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a generalization-detail-generalization includes only things similar to the details.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this is so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where the rule just used comes from. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 2 depended on the rule 'only include things similar to the detail.' Before going on, the גמרא wants a source showing how this rule works.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? (asks for a source)
That it is so

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is so?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule from the last step: include only things similar to the named examples.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule used in the challenge of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things similar to the detail.

steps.title: The ברייתא on spending מעשר שני money: general, detail, general
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא breaks the מעשר שני פסוק into three parts: a generalization, a detail, and a second generalization.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'And you shall spend the money on whatever your heart desires' is a generalization. 'On cattle, sheep, wine, and strong drink' is a detail. 'And on whatever your soul asks of you' goes back and generalizes again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. The ברייתא first splits the פסוק about spending מעשר שני money into general, detail, general. The next step gives the ברייתא's conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא labels each part of the פסוק. The opening phrase is broad, the middle names specific foods and drinks, and the ending is broad again. This is the classic כלל ופרט וכלל shape. The ברייתא will use it to show we include only items similar to the named details.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא (introduces a teaching from the תנאים)
It generalized; it used a general phrase
It specified; it listed details
It went back and generalized again

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the standard model for how כלל ופרט וכלל works. It is the basis for the challenge against רבא.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְנָתַתָּ הַכֶּסֶף בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ״ — כָּלַל,
phrases.english: 'And you shall spend the money on whatever your heart desires' is a generalization,
phrases.notes: דברים 14:26. This is about money from מעשר שני, which is spent in ירושלים.

phrases.english: 'on cattle, on sheep, on wine, and on strong drink' is a detail,
'and on whatever your soul asks of you' goes back and generalizes again.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וְנָתַתָּ הַכֶּסֶף בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תְּאַוֶּה נַפְשְׁךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 3's question by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא shows the מעשר שני פסוק has the shape general, detail, general. Its conclusion, that only items similar to the detail are included, comes in step 5.

steps.title: The detail defines what the generalizations include
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that because the פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל, it includes only things similar to the listed details. Those details are things that are פרי מפרי and גידולי קרקע.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, you include only things that are like the detail. The details are things that come from something else that grew, and that grow from the ground. So the פסוק includes anything with those two features.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer. It shows what the כלל ופרט וכלל in the מעשר שני פסוק actually includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The listed items (בקר, צאן, יין, שכר) share two features: each comes from another living thing, and each grows from or is fed by the ground. Anything with both features may be bought with מעשר שני money. This is the source for the rule רב יהודה מדיסקרתא used against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A generalization, then a detail, then a generalization again
Similar to the detail
Produce from produce: something that comes from another thing that grew
Things grown from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: In a כלל ופרט וכלל, the detail sets the pattern. Only things that share the detail's features are included.

phrases.english: A generalization, a detail, and a generalization:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט:
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.
Just as the detail is clearly defined as
produce from produce and things grown from the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל פְּרִי מִפְּרִי וְגִידּוּלֵי קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: so too, everything that is produce from produce and grown from the ground is included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 4 by drawing its conclusion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא shows that a כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things like the detail, here things that are פרי מפרי and גידולי קרקע.

steps.title: Why is the second generalization needed?
steps.stepSummary: If a כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things like the detail, the last generalization seems to add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since we include only things like the detail, what does the last generalization accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule it just learned. It asks why the תורה needed to add the final generalization.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the last generalization, the פסוק would be a plain כלל ופרט. A כלל ופרט would limit us to the detail anyway. So the last כלל seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (introduces a logical problem)
We derive
The last generalization
What does it accomplish?

phrases.english: Now, since with a generalization, a detail, and a generalization
we include only things similar to the detail,
what does the last generalization accomplish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל כְּעֵין פְּרָטָא דָּיְינִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the structure of the rule just established.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the final כלל in a כלל ופרט וכלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the result is limited to things like the detail, the final כלל appears to add nothing.

steps.title: The last generalization adds similar items
steps.stepSummary: The last generalization adds everything similar to the detail, even items that are not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It accomplishes adding everything that is similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the last generalization is what lets us go beyond the listed items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without it, we would be limited to exactly the items listed. The second כלל widens the law to other items that share the detail's features.

keyTerms.meaning: To add, to include
That is similar to it

phrases.english: It accomplishes adding
everything that is similar to it.
phrases.notes: "It" means the detail: things like the listed items, even though they aren't named.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a function for the seemingly extra part
steps.terutzMaskana: The final כלל extends the law to all items similar to the detail.

steps.title: Why is the second detail needed?
steps.stepSummary: The same question is asked about פרט וכלל ופרט. If we include only things like the detail, the last detail seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: with a detail, a generalization, and a detail, we include things like the detail. So what does the last detail accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a parallel question about the opposite rule, פרט וכלל ופרט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The result is again "things like the detail." The first detail already sets that pattern. So the second detail seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
A detail, then a generalization, then a detail again
The last detail

phrases.english: And furthermore: with a detail, a generalization, and a detail
we include things similar to the detail,
so what does the last detail accomplish?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: פְּרָט וּכְלָל וּפְרָט כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט דָּיְינִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the parallel question about the mirror-image rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the final פרט in a פרט וכלל ופרט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first פרט already defines the pattern, so the final פרט seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The last detail keeps the generalization from widening
steps.stepSummary: Without the last detail, the generalization would expand the first detail to include everything. The last detail limits it to things like the detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the last detail, I would have said that the generalization is added onto the detail and widens it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the last detail is needed to hold back the generalization.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain פרט וכלל means the generalization widens the detail to include everything. The last פרט stops this full widening. It keeps the law to things similar to the detail.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for
I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)
A generalization that adds onto the detail

phrases.english: If not for the last detail,
I would have said:
the generalization becomes an addition to the detail.
phrases.notes: He means the general word would stretch the law to cover everything, not just things like the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו פְּרָטָא בָּתְרָאָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra part blocks a mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the final פרט, the כלל would widen the detail to include everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: The final פרט limits the law to things similar to the detail.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two rules?
steps.stepSummary: Both כלל ופרט וכלל and פרט וכלל ופרט include only things like the detail. So the גמרא asks what difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, with two generalizations and a detail, and with two details and a generalization, we include things like the detail. So what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two rules. It is setting up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After steps 5-9, both rules seem to give the same result: things similar to the detail. If so, why are they counted as two separate rules? The גמרא wants to find where they actually lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: Two generalizations and a detail (another name for כלל ופרט וכלל)
Two details and a generalization (another name for פרט וכלל ופרט)
Between this and that

steps.confusionAlert: "Two generalizations and a detail" does not mean a new rule. It is just another way of saying כלל ופרט וכלל, and "two details and a generalization" means פרט וכלל ופרט.

phrases.english: And now, since with two generalizations and a detail
and with two details and a generalization
we include things similar to the detail,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, but the corrected wording leaves it out.

phrases.english: what difference is there between this and that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on both answers. Since both rules now seem to give the same result, the גמרא asks how they differ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between כלל ופרט וכלל and פרט וכלל ופרט

steps.title: How two generalizations differ from two details
steps.stepSummary: With two generalizations and one detail, an item similar in even one way is included. With two details and one generalization, an item must be similar in two ways to be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference. With two generalizations and a detail, if an item resembles the detail even in one way, we include it. With two details and a generalization, we include an item only if it resembles the details in two ways. If it is similar in only one way, we do not include it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. Both methods include only things like the detail, but they set a different bar for how similar an item must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In כלל ופרט וכלל the two generalizations pull toward including more, so similarity in one way is enough. In פרט וכלל ופרט the two details pull toward limiting, so an item must match in two ways. The difference is how strict the test of 'similar' is.

keyTerms.meaning: Two generalizations and one detail (the pattern of כלל ופרט וכלל)
Two details and one generalization (the pattern of פרט וכלל ופרט)
In one aspect or way
In two aspects or ways
We include

phrases.english: There is a difference, for whereas
with two generalizations and a detail,
phrases.notes: This is the כלל ופרט וכלל from step 10: one detail with a generalization on each side.

phrases.english: if there is an item that resembles it
even in one aspect, we include it;
but with two details and a generalization,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִיכָּא פְּרָטָא דְּדָמֵי מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין — מְרַבִּינַן,
phrases.english: if there is an item that resembles it in two aspects, we include it;
in only one aspect, we do not include it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 about the difference between כלל ופרט וכלל and פרט וכלל ופרט.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כלל ופרט וכלל includes items similar in even one aspect. פרט וכלל ופרט includes only items similar in two aspects.

steps.title: Asking how detail-then-generalization differs from restriction-then-amplification
steps.stepSummary: Both פרט וכלל and מיעט וריבה seem to include everything, so the גמרא asks what difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, with a detail followed by a generalization, the generalization is added onto the detail and everything is included. With a restriction followed by an amplification, the amplification also includes everything, so again everything is included. So what is the difference between מיעט וריבה and פרט וכלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second comparison question, this time about two methods that both seem to include everything. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In פרט וכלל the later generalization expands the detail without limit. In מיעט וריבה the amplification also seems to include everything. If both give the same result, it is unclear why they are treated as two separate methods.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, consider; it introduces a logical point the question builds on
A detail followed by a generalization; the generalization expands the detail
The generalization becomes an addition to the detail
A restriction followed by an amplification (a method of reading the Torah through ריבוי and מיעוט)
Everything is included

phrases.english: Now, with a detail and a generalization,
the generalization becomes added to the detail,
and all things are included.
And with restriction and amplification as well,
it amplified everything, and all things are included.
What difference is there between restriction and amplification
and a detail and a generalization?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the first comparison, the גמרא raises a parallel comparison between two other methods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference exists between פרט וכלל and מיעט וריבה, since both seem to include everything?

steps.title: Leaves and tendrils show the difference
steps.stepSummary: פרט וכלל includes even the leaves and tendrils of the vine. מיעט וריבה includes the tendrils but not the leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference. With a detail and a generalization, we include even the leaves and the tendrils of the vine. With restriction and amplification, tendrils are included but leaves are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12 with a practical example from the vine forbidden to a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרט וכלל truly includes everything, even the leaves. מיעט וריבה includes a lot but still leaves out something, the leaves. So מיעט וריבה is slightly narrower than פרט וכלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves of the grapevine
Tendrils or young shoots of the grapevine
Yes
No

steps.whatToRemember: Two comparisons: כלל ופרט וכלל needs similarity in one aspect, while פרט וכלל ופרט needs two. פרט וכלל includes even leaves and tendrils, while מיעט וריבה includes tendrils but not leaves.

phrases.english: There is a difference, for whereas with a detail and a generalization
we include even leaves and tendrils.
phrases.notes: He means the leaves and tendrils of the grapevine, which would then be forbidden to a נזיר.

phrases.english: But with restriction and amplification,
tendrils, yes; leaves, no.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרט וכלל includes leaves and tendrils. מיעט וריבה includes only tendrils, not leaves.

steps.title: For a נזיר alone, permitted food combines with forbidden food
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן: throughout the Torah, permitted food does not combine with forbidden food to make up the minimum amount, except for the prohibitions of a נזיר, learned from the word ״משרת״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says in the name of רבי יוחנן: for all prohibitions in the תורה, a permitted food does not combine with a forbidden food, except for the prohibitions of a נזיר, because the תורה said: ״משרת״ (anything soaked).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a statement of רבי יוחנן about mixing permitted and forbidden food. A נזיר is the one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, to be punished you must eat the minimum amount of the forbidden food itself, and permitted food mixed in does not count toward it. For a נזיר the תורה forbids ״משרת״, food soaked in grape liquid, which shows that the permitted part joins the forbidden part. So a נזיר can be liable even when the forbidden part alone is less than the minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted food combines with forbidden food to make up the minimum amount
The prohibitions written in the Torah
Except for
A person who took a vow of נזירות, who is forbidden grape products, among other things
Soaking; something soaked in grape liquid

steps.confusionAlert: 'Combine' here is not about the taste of the mixture. It means counting the permitted food toward the minimum amount needed to be punished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement opens a new discussion. It sets up a general rule for all of the תורה's prohibitions, with נזיר as a special exception.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
With regard to all prohibitions in the Torah,
a permitted food does not combine with a forbidden food,
phrases.notes: Combining means reaching the minimum amount needed to be punished, like a כזית.

phrases.english: except for the prohibitions of a nazir,
as the Torah said: "soaked."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the comparison of the methods of reading the Torah ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all Torah prohibitions, permitted food does not combine with forbidden food toward the minimum amount, except for a נזיר, learned from ״משרת״.
